meta.title: Import Disk to LXC | ProxMenux Documentation
meta.description: Attach a physical disk to an existing LXC container on Proxmox VE using ProxMenux. Handles filesystem detection / formatting, mount point, unprivileged → privileged conversion and persistent device paths.
meta.ogTitle: Import Disk to LXC | ProxMenux Documentation
meta.ogDescription: Attach a physical disk to an existing LXC container. Handles filesystem, mount point and unprivileged → privileged conversion.

header.title: Import Disk to LXC
header.description: Attach a physical disk to an existing LXC container on the Proxmox host. ProxMenux detects free disks, optionally formats them with a supported filesystem, and wires the partition to a mount point inside the container using persistent device paths.

intro.title: VM passthrough vs LXC passthrough
intro.body: LXC passthrough is not a raw block device. The container gets a mount point — i.e. a directory backed by a partition you pick on the host. Unlike a VM, the guest kernel is the host kernel, so the filesystem (ext4 / xfs / btrfs) is read and managed by Proxmox itself and then exposed to the container.

howRuns.heading: How the script runs
howRuns.body: The flow has two phases with clear separation between "collecting information and decisions" and "actually changing the container config". Until the last dialog is answered, nothing is changed on the host or in the CT.
howRuns.summary: ProxMenux hides the root disk and other mounted disks, ZFS members, active RAID members, disks used by host LVM and disks already in this container. Disks referenced by another VM or CT are shown as ⚠ In use, and RAID / LVM signatures show a ⚠ label.

prereqs.heading: Prerequisites
items: At least one LXC container defined on the host.
The container is privileged, or you accept the script's offer to convert it.
At least one physical disk not in use by the host.
prereqs.warnBody: This script requires a privileged container for its direct disk attachment. If it detects unprivileged: 1, it offers to edit /etc/pve/lxc/<CTID>.conf in place. This changes the security model and does not remap existing file ownership. Back up the container and verify ownership before accepting, or rebuild it as privileged.

list.title: Pick the target container
list.caption: Container selection menu
list.bodyRich: ProxMenux lists the LXC containers on the host (pct list), except those created from an OCI image, whose paths are managed in the OCI manager. Pick the one that will receive the disks. If the container is unprivileged you are offered to convert it now.

list.title: Pick the physical disk
list.caption: Free disks detected on the host (with ⚠ labels for stale metadata)
list.bodyRich: Only safe candidates are shown, and you can select several disks in one run. For each disk, a running VM or CT that uses it skips the disk, a stopped one asks you to confirm, and a RAID member is refused.

list.title: Format or reuse
list.intro: For each selected disk the script inspects the first partition:
items: If it already has a filesystem, you choose to use it as-is (existing files are preserved) or format it.
If it has no filesystem, it is formatted: pick ext4 / xfs / btrfs. Formatting always asks for one more confirmation.

list.title: Pick the mount point
list.bodyRich: Type the path where the container should see the disk. ProxMenux suggests /mnt/disk_<device> (for example /mnt/disk_sdb) and adds a suffix if that path is already in use. This is the path inside the container; the host refers to the partition through /dev/disk/by-id/….

list.title: Attach and verify
list.caption: Assignment to CT
list.bodyRich: ProxMenux appends a fresh mpN: entry to the container config, skipping indexes already in use, and re-reads the config to confirm. For xfs and btrfs it also installs xfsprogs or btrfs-progs inside the container, offering to start it if it is stopped. If the container is running the mount is exec'd live; otherwise it takes effect on the next start.

important.heading: Important considerations
items: Several disks per run: select them together in the checklist; each one gets its own mount point.
Do not attach the same partition to several containers that might mount it simultaneously — concurrent writes corrupt the filesystem.
Old metadata: disks with ZFS signatures are hidden and RAID members are refused. Clear that metadata first with the Format / Wipe Physical Disk tool.

troubleshoot.heading: Troubleshooting
troubleshoot.unprivBody: You declined the conversion, so the script stopped without changing anything. To continue, run it again and accept: the script stops the container, backs up its configuration to /etc/pve/lxc/<CTID>.conf.bak and replaces unprivileged: 1 with unprivileged: 0. That flag change alone does not convert the UID/GID ownership of existing files, so back up the container and fix the ownership first; alternatively, restore or rebuild the container as privileged.
troubleshoot.permsTitle: Permissions inside the container are wrong
troubleshoot.permsBody: Existing file ownership is retained when a partition is mounted into a privileged container; a newly formatted filesystem is often owned by root:root. If the service runs as another user (e.g. www-data for Nextcloud), inspect its UID/GID and adjust the required files with chown/chmod. Changes also affect the underlying disk.
